Consult Summary:
- Female patient with 2-day history of lower abdominal pain and systemic symptoms; possible urinary tract infection; plan to start empiric antibiotics for 3 days with follow-up if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 2-day history of lower abdominal pain with feeling hot and sweaty; mild nausea without vomiting; no diarrhea.
- Symptom progression: Pain began 2 days ago; currently ongoing. Temperature self-measured around 37°C (afebrile at other times, previously reported warmth/sweats).
- Urinary symptoms: Increased frequency; slight pink color in urine reported. Pain when passing water described as not present. No back pain.
- Bowel symptoms: Recent constipation last week, now resolved; normal bowel movement about 2 hours ago.
- Other symptoms: Thirstier than normal; no acid reflux or upper abdominal pain; no vaginal bleeding or discharge reported.
- Past episodes: None prior to current episode.
- Exposures: No recent travel abroad.
- Medications: No regular medications. Over-the-counter meds not used. Contraceptive implant present for about one year; currently not on regular medications.
- Allergies: Amoxycillin (allergic reaction not specified).
- Medical history: No significant past medical problems reported.
- Social history: Lives with parents. Smokes: does not smoke. Alcohol: drinks about four beers per week.
- Family history: Mother had breast cancer, treated successfully.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected urinary tract infection (UTI) with supportive urinary symptoms and mild systemic symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Initiate a three-day course of antibiotics; specific agent not named (name not documented).
    - Dosing: twice daily for three days.
    - Start antibiotics as soon as prescription is received via pharmacy.
    - Education/follow-up: If pain worsens, fever develops, back pain occurs, or new symptoms arise, re-evaluate (possible in-person examination).
- Issue 2: Urinary symptoms with hematuria (pink urine) and increased frequency; no dysuria reported.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor symptoms; seek prompt reassessment if symptoms worsen or do not improve after antibiotic course.

General plan:
- Ensure pharmacy is set; patient is to commence antibiotics once received.
- Advise patient to contact clinic immediately if worsening symptoms or new concerns arise.
